Marta Rivera: Heads-up — customer reported a double-charge when a streaming session fell back to a secondary route and a toolcall got truncated. Spike in billing dashboard at ~21:14 UTC. :eyes:
Devon Li: Can you grab the router + billing traces? any route ids or session ids?
Marta Rivera: Quick summary: primary route -> mid-request model swap (canary) -> reconnect -> toolcall truncated -> stream resumed -> billing shows both partial toolcall and resumed stream tokens.
Sam Patel: can you paste the raw headers + router trace id? e.g. `x-route-id`, `x-session`, `x-toolcall-id` :point_down:
Marta Rivera: ```
x-route-id: r-81b6
x-session: s-cc123
x-toolcall-id: t-9abf
router-trace: tr-2026-03-21-21:14:07
```
Marta Rivera: logs snippet: ```
[21:14:07] ROUTER: FALLBACK_ROUTED route=r-82 reason=capacity_canary
[21:14:07] RUNTIME: TOOLCALL_TRUNCATED toolcall=t-9abf offset=128
[21:14:08] RUNTIME: STREAM_RESUME session=s-cc123 resume_from=prefix
[21:14:09] METERING: PROVISIONAL_CREDIT session=s-cc123 amount=120
[21:14:12] METERING: CONFIRMED_CREDIT session=s-cc123 amount=120
```
Jun O'Neill: Are we seeing provisional credits at handoff + confirmed credits after resume? that'd explain double-charge. Need durable dedupe key for the ledger.
Casey Gomez: telemetry currently tags events with `billing_status: provisional|confirmed`, but router sometimes emits both for the same session_id after a resume. We need a composite unique id to dedupe across provisional->confirmed transitions.
Devon Li: Proposal: composite dedupe key = `session_id + toolcall_id + prefix_offset`. Also emit `handoff_state` in router events (e.g., `superseded`, `final`) so metering can decide. Console should surface provisional vs final in the trace timeline.
Ralph Chen: Console UX note: product asked for a simpler surface — show a single 'billing impact pending' badge in the timeline with an expandable detail for power users. keep the main view clean.
Marta Rivera: @Devon quick mitigation: when fallback happens mid-toolcall, mark the original toolcall as `superseded` (not `confirmed`) until we get a final commit from the ledger. avoids provisional->confirmed double-count. :thumbsup:
Devon Li: I'll prototype in router: add `handoff_state: superseded` and emit only one final `billing-confirm` event after ledger ack. need to coordinate with metering team and ensure existing customers don't break. :calendar:
billing-bot: Incident created: BILL-2371 duplicate provisional credit spike — assigned to @Devon Li, @Casey Gomez. Pager duty notified.
Sam Patel: For rollout UX — we could start canary with a `no-confirmation` mode where router suppresses provisional billing tags for N% of traffic during model swaps. gives us breathing room while model switch stabilizes.
Jun O'Neill: ops concern: that increases risk of undercharging on real faults. ops prefers charge-then-refund model so revenue is protected. need SLA decision.
Marta Rivera: agreed — make `no-confirmation` opt-in per-customer. Devon, can you sketch telemetry + console change + an internal API flag (`router.handoff.billing_mode=opt_in|always`) so product/sales can toggle per-customer? I'll sync with CS/sales after the sketch.
